title: Predicate Logic
body:
**Predicate logic** breaks a statement open into the objects it is about and the properties or
relations holding of them. Sentential logic treats a whole statement as one letter, which makes
some valid arguments invisible to it:

```
All cats are mammals.       P
Felix is a cat.             Q
So Felix is a mammal.       R        three unrelated letters, no connection to find
```

The pieces of the language:

```
constants     a, b, f      name particular objects        f = Felix
variables     x, y, z      stand in for objects, and get bound by a quantifier
predicates    C, M, L      properties and relations       Cx = x is a cat
                                                          Lxy = x loves y
```

An atomic formula is a predicate applied to the right number of terms, so `Cf` says Felix is a
cat and `Lfx` says Felix loves x. Connectives combine them exactly as before, and
[[Quantifier|quantifiers]] bind the variables. The argument above becomes:

```
∀x (Cx → Mx)
Cf
∴ Mf
```

which the quantifier rules in [[Natural Deduction]] derive in two lines. The number of
argument places is fixed per predicate, and a one-place predicate is a property while a
two-place predicate is a relation, which is what allows the logic to express orderings and
comparisons that sentential logic cannot reach.
